title: A holdout the chat already looked at is said beside its number (H8's open gap, rule 2)
request: The owner chose to close the gap the review of 2026-10-28 found: H8 carried what an analysis explored into the project, but no split or report read it.
spec: dclab_core.exposure.holdout_exposure reads the carried exposure against the split that ran (after, seen, may_hold); the final stage keeps it in its evidence and adds its note once to the holdout's claim unless the holdout was a first look; the split is never moved.
plan: Write the rule in dclab_core: names and dates only, never a value.
Read it in the final stage of every kind, its own machine included, and in the programme's record.
Tie every exposure entry to the table it was computed on, and carry only the built table's.
Test the three statuses, the engine path, a machine kind, the report and two tables.

decisions.decision: The split is never moved; the number is marked.
decisions.why: A deterministic split owns the holdout; moving it from the chat's history would make the holdout depend on what a person asked.

decisions.decision: A holdout starting the day after the answers' last date is may_hold, not after.
decisions.why: The answers read times in UTC and the split in the table's own clock; a false after is the dangerous direction.

decisions.decision: The note sits on the holdout's claim only.
decisions.why: The report lists the evidence's limits and the claims' limitations together, so it was said twice.

change: New dclab_core/exposure.py (holdout_exposure, mark_claims; dclab-core 0.133.0, CHANGELOG, CORE_INTEGRATION section, data catalog); studio/engine.py: Prepared.exposure, the final stage and a machine kind's final mark the holdout claim; studio/programme.py keeps the verdict; home_query.table_identity on every answer's and dashboard tile's exposure entry; draft/exits.conversion carries only the built table's entries; tests/test_holdout_exposure.py, test_home_exits; test_core_contracts allows Cython's _cyutility module (pandas 3, SciPy 1.17).

findings.defect: Kinds with their own machine and the programme never got the mark.
findings.scenario: Monthly sales were explored in the chat, then a forecast was built: the forecasting machine's final stage reported a clean holdout number.
findings.cause: Only the tabular stage_final read the exposure.
findings.fix: The engine marks a machine's final record after it runs (may_hold when the machine does not say its holdout's dates); the programme keeps the verdict when it reads the holdout.

findings.defect: Time zones could give a false after.
findings.scenario: A row at 02:00 at UTC+4 on the day after the answers' last date is the day before in UTC, inside what the chat read, yet the holdout was called a first look.
findings.cause: The query reads dates in UTC; the engine keeps the table's clock.
findings.fix: after needs more than a day between the last explored date and the holdout's start; the day after is may_hold, said with the reason.

findings.defect: What was explored on one table was said about a project built on another.
findings.scenario: Answers on table A related plan to churned; table B was uploaded and built: its project was marked and told to check plan for leakage.
findings.cause: An exposure entry did not say which table it was computed on.
findings.fix: Every entry keeps its asset and table hash; the conversion carries only the built table's (an unnamed old entry only when the draft never had another table).

findings.defect: The report printed the note twice.
findings.scenario: The project built after a chat that saw its holdout showed the same sentence twice in the report's limits.
findings.cause: The note was in the evidence's limits and in the holdout claim's limitations.
findings.fix: mark_claims adds it once, to the holdout's claim.

outcome: Every holdout number of a project built after an analysis says whether the chat already looked at its rows, once and in plain words, without moving the split.
lessons: Two readers of one date column must agree on its clock before they compare: when they do not, keep a margin on the safe side.
risks: A machine that does not report its holdout's dates is always may_hold, which can mark a holdout the chat never reached.
